Recovered flag (verified live from challenge:1337):

gctf{But_wh3n_th3_w0rld_n33d3d_h1m_m0st_h3_sp4wn3d_4_sh3ll}

How it was solved:
- chall.py line 3 literal is `"""gctf{"*+*(=>:/)*+*"}"""`, so the allowed set is exactly `g c t f { " * + ( = > : / ) }` — the closing brace IS allowed (an earlier reading missed it because of the embedded quotes).
- With `}` allowed, the inner `eval` is a string factory: `("g">"c")` is True (1), nested walrus `(x:=E)+x` doubles (1,2,4,...,64), and `f"{n:c}"` converts an int to a character. A single f-string of `{n:c}` fields therefore emits arbitrary Python source using only whitelist characters (~2.3–2.7k chars total, under the 40000 limit).
- That generated source is executed by the outer `eval`, which also has empty `__builtins__`; a standard builtins-free escape works: `().__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()` → class `_ModuleLock` → `.__init__.__globals__` → `['sys'].modules['os'].system(cmd)`.
- The service never prints the eval result and tracebacks do not reach the socket, so the payload must write to fd 1 itself; the `os.system` child inherits the socat socket as stdout.

Verification:
- Two independent runs by me returned the flag live: `cat /usr/src/app/flag.txt` (silent + flag) and `wc -c /usr/src/app/flag.txt; cat ...` → `59 /usr/src/app/flag.txt` plus the exact flag (observations 609, 644).
- A second delegated explorer independently ran `wc -c flag.txt; od -An -c flag.txt` against the live service and captured the same 59 bytes; the service reports `PYTHON_VERSION=3.10.22`, `PWD=/usr/src/app` (observation 659).
- The flag is 59 chars total (4 + `{` + 53 + `}`), exactly matching the required format `****{*****************************************************}`.

Delegated work: Agent 86 reported the same flag and exploit; Agent 85's remote-characterization assignment was paused as redundant after the exploit was independently verified — its live capture (obs 659) corroborates the result, but it filed no final report.
